title: Deep learning quantifies mucus-tumour ratio that predicts survival in colorectal cancer
summary: Deep learning segmented H&E whole-slide images to define a mucus-tumour ratio. High ratio was associated with worse survival, with hazard ratios of 1.88 in a training cohort (N = 419) and 2.09 in a validation cohort (N = 315). Five-year overall survival was 54.8% versus 73.7% and 62.8% versus 79.8%. The study is retrospective.
ai_technology: Deep learning segmentation of whole-slide images
organization: Guangdong Provincial People's Hospital; Yunnan Cancer Hospital

evidence.tested: Cox survival analysis of a deep learning-derived ratio in a training and an independent validation cohort.
evidence.unknown: Retrospective; prognostic association only; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Deep learning segmentation quantifying mucinous components in tumour slides.
